note: *fez maravilhoso o seu santo*, as Matos Soares 1932. The stylist's *fez maravilhas pelo seu santo* was refused (D8) as the Hebrew's sense, not the Latin's; it stays an option, with *tornou admirável*.
*nos vossos leitos compungi-vos*: the stylist asked *arrependei-vos*, refused (D8) as another word (*pænitére*) that drops the sting. The blind reader did not know *compungi-vos*.

*eles se multiplicaram* was supplied (D8) so the verb would not be heard of the produce; the blind reader of draft 3 still heard it of *trigo, vinho e azeite*. Pending: an order that ties *eles* to the people.
*in idípsum* → *a um só tempo* stands only for now: D9 defers the phrase (six places) to its own word study. *juntamente* and *nisso mesmo* are the options.
*vós, Senhor, a sós na esperança*: the stylist's *só vós* was refused (D8) because it closes an ambiguity the Latin leaves open. *singularmente* is the other option.
